policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Here, moreover, it is required' opens with the adverb 'Here', rendering ὧδε; the RP relative Ὃ δὲ ('Moreover what is sought') leaves no word for 'Here' and restructures the clause.
Ἀπολλῶν and Ἀπολλὼ are alternative accusative forms of the same name; ASV 'Apollos' renders either identically.
ASV 'not to go beyond the things which are written' has a plural relative and plural verb agreement in the English phrase, matching the plural ἃ; the singular ὃ would yield 'that which is written'.
ASV ends the clause at 'the things which are written' with nothing answering to φρονεῖν ('to be minded'), so the RP addition is unrendered.

ASV takes δοκῶ parenthetically ('For, I think, God hath set forth'); English regularly drops the complementizer 'that', so the presence or absence of ὅτι is not distinguished by the wording, and the chapter's only note here is an alternative_rendering about 'to angels, and to men'.
δυσφημούμενοι and βλασφημούμενοι are synonyms here and ASV 'being defamed' renders either; the verse note ('Or, refuse') is an alternative_rendering touching 'offscouring', not this word.

ASV has one finite verb, 'I write', with 'but to admonish you' subordinate to it — the participial νουθετῶν; the indicative νουθετῶ would give a second finite clause, 'but as my beloved children I admonish you'.
The variant is Greek word order only; ASV 'my beloved and faithful child' renders μου τέκνον and τέκνον μου alike.
ASV reads 'my ways which are in Christ' with no 'Jesus', so the name is absent from the text rendered.
